claim_en: daber ('speak'), opening the holiness charge: 'with TWO geresh strokes' (gershayim, the double back-slanted accent) — in-stream.

ha-elilim ('the idols'): MS rules 'the he with GALGAL (the wheel-accent)'; SNAPSHOT writes the munach (the upright conjunctive stroke) — galgal-class station 6, the camps splitting exactly as at the anointed priest's im (Lev 4:3).

source: Minchat Shai + Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Lev 19:5 (Baal HaTurim; Chullin 31; Rambam)
claim_en: tizbachuhu ('you shall slaughter it') written LEAN — no vav after the chet — the Baal HaTurim: 'that two should not slaughter one sacrifice.' MS notes the halakha runs the OTHER way (the sages of Chullin: two MAY slaughter one offering; Rambam so rules) — the lean skeleton carries the rejected opinion. Once in the Torah.

source: Minchat Shai on Lev 19:6 quoting the Ramah
claim_en: The Ramah's left-over rule: 'every notar-word (left over) in the Torah is FULL with vav, except ONE lean — ve-hanotar of the Passover night, parashat ha-chodesh.' The single lean skeleton stands exactly at Exod 12:10, his own sign.

source: Minchat Shai on Lev 19:6 quoting the Ramah
claim_en: The rule's full side: ve-hanotar with the vav stands six times — the peace-offering pair (7:16/17), the investiture (8:32), the poor leper's oil twice (14:18/29), and this verse's third-day remainder.
ki ('for') in 'for he has profaned the LORD's holy thing': 'with MAQQEF (the joining stroke), not with tevir (the broken third-rank pause)' — SNAPSHOT joins MS's camp: the stroke is in-stream.
et chukotai tishmoru ('MY STATUTES you shall keep'): 'so it is written — the mem with HOLAM (the o-dot), not with sheva' — the rare o-pointed keep-verb, in-stream.
ve-hi ('and she') of the bondwoman case: 'written with VAV and pointed with chiriq (the i-dot)' — the written-vav/read-yod class, the she-word wearing the he-word's skeleton, in-stream.
ve-hafdeh ('and she shall be redeemed'): 'the he with qamatz ALONE (no stress-stroke) and the dalet DAGESHED (the hardening dot)' — the dagesh checked, the bare qamatz asserted at build.

source: Minchat Shai on Lev 19:25 (the Hilleli and Yerushalmi codices; the Meiri; the Ramah)
claim_en: ha-chamishit ('the fifth [year]'): the Hilleli codex wrote it doubly FULL; the Yerushalmi codex and the Masorah rule full-first-yod-lean-second, 'and it is marked UNIQUE — nothing else written so' — the Meiri and all precise books concur, the shin soft (asserted). SNAPSHOT with the Masorah against the Hilleli: the unique form stands here alone.

source: Minchat Shai on Lev 19:25 quoting the Ramah
claim_en: The Ramah's fifth-word ledger, other classes: 'chamishit doubly FULL — two, sign: the fifth to Pharaoh, and he shall add the fifth of the Sanctifier's redemption' — exactly the two doubly-full stations in the stream (Gen 47:24, Lev 27:15); the lean-first class (Lev 27:19) asserted at build.

tevuato ('ITS produce' — the tree's): written with final VAV; 'chumashim that write it with he are in plain error' — the he-for-vav endings exist only twice in Scripture, both in the Prophets (Jer 2:3, Ezek 48:18, outside the instrument). The vav-form stands once in the Torah, here.

The chapter's dagesh pair: me-Elohekha ('[fear] your God', 19:32) — 'the mem DAGESHED'; ha-ger ('the stranger', 19:34) — 'the gimel DAGESHED' (checked and asserted respectively) — both hardening dots in-stream.

'FOUR reaping-words in the verse' — to exclude the four lost harvests: robbers reaped it, ants nibbled it, wind broke it, cattle ate it. The verse carries exactly four reap-root tokens (asserted at build by root; no span-count check type yet).

'TEN times the-LORD-your-God in this portion' — the Kedoshim portion (Lev 19-20) carries EXACTLY TEN adjacent pairs of the Name and 'your God' (eight in ch. 19, two in ch. 20; asserted at build) — the holiness charge sealed by a minyan of Names, for 'a matter of holiness needs ten.'
